evidence.detail: Scene constructs rs/T separately from the wall object and stores it in the SceneTile wall-decoration slot.
The holder has one Renderable plus wall-relative position/orientation metadata used by Scene's decoration insertion/render path.

proposals.note: WallDecoration names the wall-attached decorative renderable holder.

evidence.detail: Scene constructs rs/n and stores it in a separate SceneTile slot from GroundDecoration and GameObject.
The holder carries three Renderable references at one tile location plus pile height/tag metadata, matching the scene's stacked ground-item rendering path.

proposals.note: GroundItemPile names the three-renderable tile pile used for stacked ground items.

evidence.detail: The constructor receives plane/x/y tile coordinates and instances are stored directly in Scene's three-dimensional tile grid.
Each tile owns the tile paint/model plus WallObject, WallDecoration, GroundDecoration, GroundItemPile and an array of GameObject references, with a linked lower/adjacent SceneTile reference.

proposals.note: SceneTile names one cell of the Scene grid and its attached scene entities.

evidence.detail: Scene constructs rs/m from one Renderable and stores it in the dedicated singleton ground-decoration slot of SceneTile.
The holder carries the centered world/tile position and tag/config state used for the floor-level decorative renderable.

proposals.note: GroundDecoration names the singleton floor-level decorative renderable attached to a SceneTile.

evidence.detail: Scene constructs rs/l for generic scene entities, records one Renderable plus orientation/tag state and tile-boundary coordinates, and installs the same object reference into every SceneTile covered by its footprint.
Each SceneTile can hold up to five rs/l references with per-object edge masks, distinguishing this role from singleton wall or ground-decoration slots.

proposals.note: GameObject is the general one-or-more-tile scene object holder.

evidence.detail: The class owns the 3D rs/H tile grid together with terrain heights, temporary game-object collections, visibility maps and occlusion state.
It creates tiles across planes, inserts/removes/queries wall, decoration, game-object and ground-object holders, performs model-normal merging and drives the scene traversal/rendering pipeline.
Client world loading uses this structure alongside the R39 CollisionMap array, separating rendered scene ownership from movement clipping.

proposals.note: Scene is the conservative semantic name for the world scene graph/controller represented by rs/V.

evidence.detail: Scene constructs rs/U and stores it in the dedicated rs/H wall slot.
The holder stores two Renderable references plus world position/orientation masks, matching a boundary wall that can expose two rendered sides.

proposals.note: WallObject describes the two-renderable boundary/wall holder attached to a SceneTile.
